newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Dutchman, Russian to contest world draughts title.
newsitem.headline: Dutchman, Russian to contest world draughts title.

text.p: A Dutch challenger and the Russian titleholder finished equal first at the end of the 18th World Draughts championships in Ivory Coast and will meet again next year to decide who is champion, the organisers said.

Dutch player Rob Clerc and Russian title holder Alexi Tchijov would meet in a play-off, probably in February 1997, at a venue to be agreed by the world federation, the organisers told Reuters after the competition ended late on Tuesday.

The two players emerged top of a group of 12 players -- 10 Europeans and two Ivorians -- who qualified for the final stages of the championship which began in this Francophone West African nation on November 6.
A second Russian, Alexander Schwarzman, finished in third place.
A total of 40 players from 21 countries from Europe, Asia, the Americas and Africa took part in the preliminary phases of the competition.
Ten qualified for the final phases, which began on November 15, along with Tchijov and the reigning vice-champion, fellow Russian Gountis Valmeris.
The 17th championships took place in 1994 in The Hague in the Netherlands.
